at_black_mountain.significance: Josef Albers was a pivotal figure in establishing the art curriculum at Black Mountain College.

Josef Albers.summary: Josef Albers was a German-born American artist and educator known for his work in color theory and geometric abstraction. He played a crucial role in shaping the art education at Black Mountain College.

at_black_mountain.significance: Katherine Dreier supported Black Mountain College through her advocacy for modern art and her involvement with the Société Anonyme.

Dreier.summary: Katherine Dreier was an influential art patron who supported modern art and Black Mountain College, notably through her work with the Société Anonyme.

at_black_mountain.significance: Josef Albers was a pivotal figure at Black Mountain College, where he taught and influenced the development of modern art education.

Albers.summary: Josef Albers was a German-American artist and educator known for his work in color theory and abstract art. He was a key faculty member at Black Mountain College, shaping its art program.

major_works.title: I Came Out of the Eighteenth Century

John Andrew Rice.summary: John Andrew Rice was an American educator and the founder of Black Mountain College. He was instrumental in establishing the college's progressive educational philosophy.

Hamilton Holt.summary: Hamilton Holt was an American educator and editor who played a key role in the founding of Black Mountain College. He served as the college's first president and was known for his progressive educational ideas.

at_black_mountain.significance: Ted Dreier was a co-founder of Black Mountain College and played a key role in its administration and financial management.

at_black_mountain.significance: Anni Albers was a pioneering textile artist who taught at Black Mountain College and influenced modern textile design.

Anni Albers.summary: Anni Albers was a German-American textile artist and printmaker known for her innovative work in textile design. She taught at Black Mountain College and significantly influenced modern art and design.

at_black_mountain.significance: Heinrich Jalowetz contributed to the music program at Black Mountain College, bringing European musical traditions to the institution.

Heinrich Jalowetz.summary: Heinrich Jalowetz was an Austrian conductor and musicologist who taught at Black Mountain College. He was instrumental in developing the college's music curriculum until his death in 1946.

at_black_mountain.significance: Natasha Goldowski was a scientist and chemist at Black Mountain College, known for her work until her lab burned down in 1948.

at_black_mountain.significance: John Dewey visited and supported Black Mountain College, influencing its educational philosophy with his progressive ideas.

at_black_mountain.significance: John A. Rice was the founder of Black Mountain College and a key figure in its educational philosophy.

John A. Rice.summary: John A. Rice was an American educator and founder of Black Mountain College, known for his progressive educational ideas. His leadership helped shape the college's innovative approach to learning.

at_black_mountain.significance: Robert Wunsch was instrumental in developing the drama program at Black Mountain College during its formative years.

Wunsch.summary: Robert Wunsch was a drama teacher at Black Mountain College from 1933 to 1945. He played a key role in establishing the college's drama department.

at_black_mountain.significance: Paul Goodman was a visiting faculty member known for his influence on social criticism and education.

Paul Goodman.summary: Paul Goodman was an American writer and social critic known for his works on education and social issues. He was a visiting faculty member at Black Mountain College during 1950-1951.

biography.death_place: New York City, New York, USA

Merce Cunningham.summary: Merce Cunningham was an iconic American dancer and choreographer who revolutionized modern dance. He taught at Black Mountain College, where he developed his innovative approach to choreography.

at_black_mountain.significance: Fuller taught at Black Mountain College where he developed the concept of the geodesic dome.

Buckminster Fuller.summary: Buckminster Fuller was an American architect, systems theorist, author, designer, and inventor. He is best known for popularizing the geodesic dome and his work at Black Mountain College.

biography.death_place: New York City, New York, USA

at_black_mountain.significance: John Cage was a leading avant-garde composer who taught at Black Mountain College, where he developed his experimental approach to music.

biography.death_place: New York City, New York, USA

at_black_mountain.significance: Monteux contributed to the music program at Black Mountain College.

at_black_mountain.significance: Max Dehn was a mathematician who taught at Black Mountain College, contributing to its interdisciplinary approach to education.

at_black_mountain.significance: Walter Gropius was a founder of the Bauhaus School and influenced Black Mountain College through his architectural and educational philosophies.

Walter Gropius.summary: Walter Gropius was a pioneering architect and founder of the Bauhaus School, known for his modernist designs. His influence extended to Black Mountain College through his innovative educational and architectural ideas.

at_black_mountain.significance: Breuer was influential in introducing modernist architecture to the college.

Kenneth Noland.summary: Kenneth Noland was an American painter known for his abstract work. He studied at Black Mountain College from 1946 to 1948, where he developed his signature style.

at_black_mountain.significance: Robert Motherwell was an influential instructor who brought his expertise in abstract expressionism to Black Mountain College.

Robert Motherwell.summary: Robert Motherwell was a leading figure in the abstract expressionist movement and an influential teacher at Black Mountain College. His work is characterized by bold forms and a deep engagement with political themes.

at_black_mountain.significance: Eric Bentley was a prominent theatre critic and playwright associated with Black Mountain College.

Eric Bentley.summary: Eric Bentley was a renowned theatre critic and playwright known for his work on Bertolt Brecht. He was associated with Black Mountain College during its operation.
